title: Flash Freeze Fruit Flies in Liquid Nitrogen
author: Rita M. Graze
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.nr3dd8n

steps.title: Count and label virgin vials
steps.instruction: Count the number of virgin flies placed in each collection vial and write this number on the outside of the vial.

steps.title: Check for larvae and consolidate
steps.instruction: Inspect each virgin collection vial for larvae; if none are present, consolidate all flies of the same cross identifier (E#) into a single vial and write the total number of flies for that cross on the vial.

steps.title: Create tracking spreadsheet
steps.instruction: Create a spreadsheet that records, for every sample, the experiment title, block number, date, genotype, sex, V# (order number), E#, number of flies, and the planned location in both the freezer box and the –80 °C freezer.

steps.title: Verify virginity again
steps.instruction: Before starting the freeze, re‑check all virgin collection vials to confirm that they contain only virgins.

steps.title: Pre‑label freezer box
steps.instruction: Write on the outside of the freezer box the experiment title, block number (if multiple blocks), date, your name and email.

steps.title: Pre‑label cryovials
steps.instruction: On each cryovial write the V# (starting at 1 for the order the vials will be frozen), E# (cross identifier), sex, genotype, block number, date, and later add the exact number of flies frozen. Use any shorthand you prefer, but document the full meaning in the spreadsheet.

steps.title: Mark bench timing tape
steps.instruction: Place a strip of tape on the bench to note the time each tube should be frozen; allow flies 15 minutes to relax after being pounded through the funnel into the cryovial.

steps.title: Prepare liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Obtain liquid nitrogen at the chosen start time (e.g., 3 p.m.) and pour it into a rectangular Styrofoam tub large enough to hold two freezer boxes. Remember that all flies must be frozen within a 2‑hour window.

steps.title: Arrange multi‑genotype order
steps.instruction: If freezing multiple genotypes, intermix vials so that no single genotype is frozen consecutively; a simple method is to freeze all vials of the first replicate, then all of the second replicate, and so on.

steps.title: Assign personnel for large freezes
steps.instruction: For large freezes, have two or more people seated in front of the racks and freeze vials from left to right, front to back, each person handling the vials in their section.

steps.title: Transfer flies to cryovials
steps.instruction: For non‑anesthetic freezes, select a pre‑labeled cryovial and the corresponding virgin vial, pound the flies through a funnel into the cryovial, and screw the lid on loosely but securely. For CO₂‑anesthetized freezes, knock out the flies, count them on a pad, sweep them into the cryovial, and screw the lid on loosely but securely.

substeps.instruction: Non‑anesthetic: pound flies through funnel into cryovial; loosely secure lid.
CO₂‑anesthetic: knock‑out, count, sweep into cryovial; loosely secure lid.

steps.title: Time and submerge cryovials
steps.instruction: Place each cryovial on the taped bench and note the time (group vials in 5‑minute blocks). Approximately 15 minutes later, move the cryovials to the liquid‑nitrogen‑filled freezer box in order of V# from left to right, front to back, submerging each vial quickly; use tweezers to first dip the vial into the nitrogen at the side of the box, then position it in its final slot.

substeps.instruction: Record placement time on tape, grouping by 5‑minute intervals.
After ~15 minutes, transfer vials to the LN₂ box in V# order.
Use tweezers to submerge each vial quickly and place it in the correct slot.

steps.title: Post‑freeze organization and record
steps.instruction: After the vials are frozen, optionally rearrange them with tweezers to group by replicate or type, but ensure the spreadsheet records the exact location of each cryovial (e.g., A1 = row A, column 1).
